conversation.content:
Hi there—thank you for taking a few minutes to talk with me. My name is Maya, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician who works with new moms. I’m here to do a quick check-in using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS). It’s a 10-question tool that helps us see how you’ve been feeling emotionally and physically during the past week, so we can make sure you’re getting the right support in these early weeks of motherhood. Everything you share stays between us unless you give permission otherwise or there’s an urgent safety concern. We’ll go through one question at a time, and there are no right or wrong answers—just whatever feels true for you. Ready to start?

Question 1: In the past seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things as much as you usually would, or has that felt harder?

I... I guess it's felt harder. I used to laugh a lot with my partner—little inside jokes, silly memes—but lately it’s like the jokes just bounce off me. I’ll smile to be polite, but inside I feel flat, like I’m watching life through fogged glass.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
No, not really… I mean, I can force a little chuckle if someone says something funny, but it feels kind of fake. Nothing seems truly funny anymore.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not much. I used to get excited about little plans—coffee with a friend, a walk, even just a quiet shower—but now it all feels like another chore. I still do them, but I’m not really looking forward to anything; I’m just going through the motions.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I do that a lot. If the baby won’t settle, I immediately think it’s because I’m doing something wrong—like I’m not feeding him right or holding him the “correct” way. The other night he cried for an hour straight and I kept replaying every little thing I’d done, convinced it was my fault. My partner kept saying babies just cry, but I still felt like I was failing him somehow.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes, pretty much every day. I’ll be sitting there and suddenly my chest feels tight, thinking the baby might stop breathing or that I’ll drop him. Sometimes I check on him five, six times an hour just to be sure he’s okay. I know there’s no real reason, but I can’t shake the fear.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yeah… it hits out of nowhere. Like yesterday, I was folding laundry and suddenly felt like the walls were closing in—heart racing, couldn’t catch my breath. I knew there wasn’t any danger, but my body was screaming that something awful was about to happen. It passed after a few minutes, but it left me shaky the rest of the day.
Things have been getting on top of me

They really have. Some mornings I wake up already exhausted, thinking about the feeds, the diapers, the laundry, the texts I haven’t answered—and it feels like I’m drowning in it. I keep lists, but even crossing things off doesn’t help much; new stuff just piles on. I manage the basics, but it’s like I’m barely treading water most days.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes. I lie down and my mind just keeps spinning—playing back every little thing I think I did wrong, worrying about what tomorrow will look like. Even when the baby’s asleep, I can’t drift off. I’ll stare at the ceiling for hours or wake up at 3 a.m. and can’t get back to sleep. I’m exhausted, but the sadness and worries keep buzzing.
I have felt sad or miserable

That’s pretty much how I feel most of the time. It’s like there’s a gray cloud hanging over everything. I’ll look at the baby and feel love, but it’s quickly followed by this heavy sadness I can’t shake. Little tasks feel huge, and some afternoons I just sit on the couch fighting back tears for no clear reason.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… I’ve cried three, maybe four times this week. Sometimes it’s because I feel overwhelmed, sometimes it’s nothing specific—just this wave of sadness that bursts out. Yesterday I was making oatmeal and started sobbing over the pot. My partner walked in and I couldn’t even explain why.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, I haven’t had any thoughts like that. I feel low, but I’ve never wanted to hurt myself—I just want to feel better so I can be the mom my baby needs.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 26: Screening note – Edinburg Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) responses reviewed:

Symptoms/behavioural indicators endorsed:
- Marked anhedonia (Q1, Q2)
- Persistent low mood, frequent crying (Q8, Q9)
- Excessive guilt/self-blame regarding infant care (Q3)
- Daily, non-specific anxiety with panic spells (Q4, Q5)
- Subjective sense of being overwhelmed/drowning in tasks (Q6)
- Sleep initiation/maintenance problems clearly linked to low mood/racing worries (Q7)

Pattern: Consistent depressive and anxiety-related complaints beginning post-delivery, no prior self-harm ideation reported (Q10 denied).

Risk factors noted:
✓ Depressed mood with loss of pleasure  
✓ Guilt/feelings of inadequacy as a mother  
✓ Anxiety symptoms including panic episodes  
✓ Functional sleep impairment secondary to mood  
✓ Absence of suicidal/self-harm thoughts at present

Screening significance: High endorsement of items consistent with postpartum depression and comorbid anxiety; no immediate safety concerns identified. Further clinical evaluation recommended.
